task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 for ISS-0896. The fixed code (5 e2e Playwright specs) cannot be run live in this environment (no browser/backend/Keycloak) -- but the NEW shared helper this fix introduces, getMasterAdminToken(request: APIRequestContext) in web/tests/e2e/helpers.ts, has genuinely unit-testable logic: it must call resolveCredential for username/password (env var if set, 'admin'/'admin' fallback if not), POST a fixed client_id: 'admin-cli' form body to the master token endpoint via the injected request object, and throw on a non-2xx response. Write a real vitest unit test at web/tests/unit/e2e-helpers/get-master-admin-token.test.ts (new directory, or reuse an existing web/tests/unit subdirectory if one already tests web/tests/e2e/helpers.ts -- check first) that mocks APIRequestContext.post (a fake object with a post method returning a controllable {ok, status, json} shape, no real network) and asserts: (1) with KC_ADMIN_USER/KC_ADMIN_PASSWORD unset, the POST body's username/password are 'admin'/'admin'; (2) with both env vars set, the POST body's username/password match the env values, not the fallback; (3) on a non-ok response, the function throws (and the thrown error does not itself leak the attempted username/password in its message, matching SECURITY-REVIEWER's own PASS finding); (4) on an ok response, the function returns the access_token from the JSON body.

Because getMasterAdminToken is a NEW function (no pre-fix version existed to run the test against -- WF-03's own 'pre-fix failure is non-existence' rule applies), the fail-then-pass proof must come from MUTATION rather than a literal pre-fix/post-fix run: apply at least 2 targeted mutants to the shipped helper (e.g. mutant A: hardcode username/password back to literal 'admin'/'admin' ignoring resolveCredential entirely -- must fail test (2); mutant B: remove the throw-on-non-ok check -- must fail test (3)), run the test suite against each mutant, record which specific tests fail for each, then revert every mutation and verify `git status --porcelain web/` is empty and the suite re-runs green. State this all explicitly in result.summary per WF-03's mutation-testing procedure (see docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md's 'When the pre-fix failure is code under test does not exist' section -- artifacts_in intentionally does not repeat it here, read it there). Use a throwaway git worktree for applying mutants if you can, to avoid mutating the working checkout at all; otherwise revert in place and verify.
acceptance_criteria: a real, runnable vitest unit test exists for getMasterAdminToken covering the 4 behaviors listed above
at least 2 targeted mutants were applied and each one's specific test failure(s) recorded
every mutation was reverted and the revert verified (git status --porcelain web/ empty, suite re-runs green) before this handoff completes
the thrown-error-on-failure path is confirmed not to leak the attempted credential value in its message

result.summary:
Wrote web/tests/unit/e2e-helpers/get-master-admin-token.test.ts (new directory -- no prior web/tests/unit subdirectory tested helpers.ts's getMasterAdminToken specifically; resolveCredential.test.ts and iss-0706-e2e-health-precondition.test.ts already covered other exports of the same file, so this is a sibling, not a duplicate). 4 tests, all passing against the shipped code (`npx vitest run tests/unit/e2e-helpers/get-master-admin-token.test.ts` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 4 passed (4)'): TC-1 env vars unset -> POST form username/password are 'admin'/'admin'; TC-2 env vars set -> POST form username/password match the env values, not the fallback; TC-3 non-ok response -> throws, and the thrown message is asserted to contain '401' but NOT the attempted username/password markers ('leaky-user-marker'/'leaky-password-marker'); TC-4 ok response -> returns access_token from the JSON body.

getMasterAdminToken is a NEW function -- no pre-fix version exists to run a literal pre-fix/post-fix proof against (WF-03's non-existence rule applies). Fail-then-pass proof was done via mutation, in a throwaway git worktree (`git worktree add ../letflow-mutant-wt HEAD`, node_modules symlinked in rather than reinstalled) so the working checkout was never mutated at all:

Mutant A (hardcode username/password back to literal 'admin'/'admin', bypassing resolveCredential entirely, in the worktree's web/tests/e2e/helpers.ts): re-ran the 4-test suite -> 3 passed, 1 failed. Failing test: TC-2 ('env vars set -> POSTs the env-var credentials, not the fallback'), with actual failure `expected 'admin' to be 'real-master-admin'`. TC-1/TC-3/TC-4 still passed (TC-1 happens to still pass since the mutant's hardcoded values equal the fallback values it's supposed to produce anyway).

Mutant B (removed the `if (!response.ok()) { ... throw ... }` block entirely): re-ran the 4-test suite -> 3 passed, 1 failed. Failing test: TC-3 ('non-ok response -> throws, without leaking the attempted username/password'), with actual failure `expected 'Cannot read properties of undefined (...)' to contain '401'` -- the mutant still throws (TypeError from reading .access_token off undefined json), but not the specific, status-carrying error TC-3 requires, so the test correctly still catches the mutant. TC-1/TC-2/TC-4 still passed.

Both mutants reverted: mutant A reverted via targeted Edit before mutant B was applied; the whole worktree (including mutant B) was then discarded via `git checkout -- web/tests/e2e/helpers.ts` inside the worktree, followed by `git status --porcelain web/` (worktree) showing empty except the untracked new test-file copy, and the suite re-run green (4/4 passed) against the restored code. The worktree was then removed (`git worktree remove ../letflow-mutant-wt --force`; `git worktree list` no longer shows it). Final check in the actual working checkout: `git status --porcelain web/` shows only the new test file (`?? web/tests/unit/e2e-helpers/`), no other web/ files touched, and the suite re-run there is also green (4/4 passed). The main checkout was never mutated at any point -- all mutation happened only in the throwaway worktree.
